lessons: Deferred MINOR: bank Excel/.xls export path + OFX caveat (no Israeli bank exports OFX natively).
Deferred MINOR: BOI representative-rate has no value on non-business days; carry forward prior rate.
Deferred: itemized fee sub-types עמלת ערוץ ישיר / דמי ניהול / ריבית חובה.

CRITICAL FIXED: the Step 7 reconciliation bridge had BOTH timing-item signs inverted, identically in Hebrew and English. Outstanding cheques are already deducted in the books so reaching the bank balance requires ADDING them; deposits in transit must be SUBTRACTED. Fees and interest were signed correctly, which made the block look authoritative. Derived the correct direction from first principles before changing it. Replaced the memorise-the-signs hedge with a direction test the reader can apply.

CRITICAL FIXED: the bridge was unbuildable even once corrected, because no source was given for the book opening balance, book closing balance or bank closing balance, and the mapper discarded account.balance. Added explicit sourcing plus the point that account.balance is the CURRENT balance at scrape time, not a period-end closing balance, so it is the wrong number for a month-end reconciliation. Added an opening-plus-receipts-minus-payments proof.

CRITICAL FIXED: the only credential template shown was Hapoalim's {userCode,password}, while the description and examples centre on Leumi, Discount and Mizrahi, which use {username,password} and {id,password,num}. Added a per-provider field table and a field-map builder.

CRITICAL FIXED: bank-config.json shipped "${BANK_PASSWORD}" as a JSON value. JSON does not expand environment variables, so the scraper sent the literal placeholder as the password, guaranteeing failed logins that count toward account lockout. Credentials are now built in code from the environment and the builder throws on a missing field.

CRITICAL FIXED: the priority-1 exact-reference rule compared txn.identifier (a number) with === against a string ledger reference, so it could never fire and every match silently degraded to the fuzzy rule. Both sides are now normalised to trimmed strings, with a non-empty guard so blank does not match blank.

CRITICAL FIXED: processedDate and status were discarded by the mapper. Pending rows mixed into a posted-balance comparison can never tie out, and createScraper takes startDate but no endDate so the scrape runs to today and drags the next period in. Added posted-only and close-the-period filters.

CRITICAL FIXED: every matching rule was 1:1 on amount, so the card-company lump-sum settlement and installment splits, both named in the skill's own Gotchas and Example 2, were unmatchable. Added a settlement-sum matcher and a bounded subset matcher for split payments, plus a warning that matching the settlement total proves the bank line and not the purchases behind it.

SECURITY: the entire treatment was one sentence about environment variables. Added a section covering what scraping actually costs: full credentials to a headless browser rather than a scoped token, bank terms-of-service and liability exposure, lockout, the truth about 2FA (there is no generic OTP option; support is per-provider and limited), and at-rest handling of the scraped data.

ADDED: the licensed alternative. Israel's Financial Information Service Law regime, supervised by the Israel Securities Authority, gives credential-free access via open interfaces and has covered business accounts since December 2023. For an ongoing business process that is the better path than scraping. Framed as ToS and risk, not illegality, since no directive prohibiting scraping outright could be verified.

STALE FIXED: cheque clearing was described as 1-3 days of float. The mechanism is a provisional credit on the clearing day that becomes final only after three further business days, so a returned cheque can reverse a deposit already matched in a prior period.

STALE FIXED: the FX step said to use the representative rate for 'the relevant date' with no convention. Added the transaction-date vs period-end distinction, the fact that no rate is published Fri/Sat/Sun/holidays so the last published rate carries forward, that publication follows the afternoon sampling window, and that the Bank of Israel disclaims legal standing for the rates.

STALE FIXED: the missing-invoice workflow ignored the allocation-number regime. Since 1 June 2026 an invoice at or above NIS 5,000 before VAT needs an allocation number or the VAT cannot be offset, so an unmatched debit over that figure needs an invoice CARRYING one, not just any invoice.

REMOVED a security risk introduced mid-edit: an earlier draft recommended the npm xlsx package for Excel imports. That distribution is the abandoned build with known advisories and would likely trip the Snyk scan in CI. Replaced with save-as-CSV guidance.

GATE: three unjustified evidence items (15.25%, the BOI rates URL, the nevo bookkeeping URL) all traced to references/domain-checklist.md. Resolved by adding sourced claims rather than deleting the file, since all three underpin skill body content too. The reviewer argued for moving the checklist out of the shipped folder as a build artifact, matching the sibling accounting skill; kept it for now because it is the only coverage contract future audits can diff against, but the context-cost argument is real and worth revisiting.
The checklist also contained 55 em-dashes, violating the project-wide ban, which no gate catches. Worth adding an em-dash grep over references/ to the pre-push routine.

CARRY (deferred): no reconciliation sign-off block (preparer, reviewer, date, statement reference), no ageing of open reconciling items, and no materiality threshold for an accepted residual. A practitioner has nothing to sign.

CARRY (deferred): bounced-cheque handling is still described mainly as a fee line; the reversal semantics (un-match the original receipt, re-debit the customer, re-open the item) are stated in the clearing gotcha but not wired into the engine.

CARRY (deferred): standing-order failure modes (indexed amount change, cancelled but still debiting, duplicate debit) are not covered. The MCP server list is unverified and one entry could not be located at all; recommending unidentified third parties for the credential-handling step should be revisited or removed.

CARRY (deferred): library drift. README now uses ESM import and requires Node >= 22.22.2, while the skill uses CommonJS require and gives no Node version. Also worth passing CompanyTypes.x rather than raw strings, which would make the skill's own camelCase warning self-enforcing.

VERIFIED UNCHANGED: VAT 18%, the 18% vs 15.25% VAT-split arithmetic (both correct against different denominators), the 7-year retention rule, and the full CompanyTypes enum. No bank the skill names has been removed. israeli-bank-scrapers remains a library with no bin, correctly used via createScraper, so the fabricated-CLI failure mode from an earlier skills-il skill is NOT present here.

VERIFIER ROUND: SKILL_HE.md had received the prose fixes (bridge, credentials, security, clearing, FX, allocation) but NOT the code fixes. A Hebrew reader still had the number-vs-string identifier bug, no processedDate, no posted-only/period filters, and no many-to-one matchers. Heading-count parity was 25/25 the whole time and hid it. Check parity on SUBSTANCE with per-symbol greps, not on heading counts.

VERIFIER ROUND: matchGroup() called an undefined combinations() helper; a generator is now inlined. The two sibling matchers also used inconsistent sign handling (one abs, one raw) against a record format where expenses are negative; both now compare magnitudes.

VERIFIER ROUND: matchCardSettlement hard-coded a 45-day rolling lookback, which sweeps in the tail of the previous cycle and produces a false difference. It now takes explicit cycleStart/cycleEnd read off the card statement, and includes transactions dated on the settlement date itself.

VERIFIER ROUND: Amex was listed as {id, card6Digits, password}; the README says {username, card6Digits, password}. Caught by checking the README directly rather than trusting the table I had just written. oneZero also needed calling out, since it does not use the username/password shape and would otherwise fall through the default branch and burn login attempts.

PROCESS: waited for BOTH panel agents before pushing this time, after the previous skill was pushed early on a green self-check and a coverage agent then returned seven criticals. The wait cost nothing and caught a real Hebrew-side gap.
